headline: Six of seven majors above their 200-day line, RSI deep in overbought, and whales quietly stacking coins onto exchanges
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's unusually clean today: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, and DOGE all sit above their 200-day moving averages, with only ADA below (77.6% down from its 12-month high, the laggard of the group). That's a broad uptrend structure, not a one-coin story. But 'above the 200-day' and 'healthy' aren't synonyms, and the momentum readings below make that distinction matter.

Every asset in the board is showing MACD above signal and RSI north of 75, with XRP at 85.6 and SOL at 83.2. That is not resting momentum, that's a market running hot across the board. BTC itself is a useful lesson in why you never quote price change without a window: it's down 1.47% on the day, up 21.7% over the week, and up 20.36% over the month. Three true numbers, three different stories. The daily red print is a pause inside a much larger move, and RSI at 80.7 on BTC (with ETH at 78.1) tells you that pause is happening from a stretched position, not a fresh one.

Positioning adds a wrinkle. Funding across BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and DOGE sits at a uniform 0.01% per 8 hours (about 11% annualized) on OKX, which is mild, not manic. But long/short account ratios are lopsided: DOGE at 3.23, SOL at 2.04, XRP at 1.58, all skewed long. Cheap funding with a crowded long book is a specific kind of setup. The liquidation windows back it up: BTC saw $14.5M in long liquidations versus $2.8M shorts over 13 hours, ETH $9.8M longs versus $3.2M shorts over 12 hours, SOL $9.5M longs versus $1.0M shorts. Longs are the side getting flushed on any wobble, which lines up with a market that ran up fast and is now shaking out late entries.

Flows are where the real tension sits. On the traditional finance side, BTC ETFs took in $307.5M on 21 Aug, part of a $1,917.8M five-session net with all five days in the same direction, a genuine sustained bid. ETH ETFs added $184.0M that day, $692.6M over five sessions, same pattern. That's real money buying through official channels. But whale wallets tell a different story over the last 24 hours: $293.98M in BTC moved net onto exchanges (inflows of $375.6M against outflows of just $81.6M), and the broader whale figure across assets shows $243.7M net onto exchanges. Zoom out to the weekly series and the picture has been flipping: the weeks ending Aug 01 and Aug 08 saw $1,108M and $232M move off exchanges respectively, but the week ending Aug 15 reversed to $508M onto exchanges, and the week ending Aug 22 shows $1,125M onto exchanges, the largest weekly onto-exchange move in the set. Coins moving toward exchanges is typically read as positioning for potential selling, and that's now been the direction for two straight weeks even as ETF buyers keep showing up. Stablecoin float, meanwhile, is essentially flat (up just 0.26% over 30 days to $308.5B), so the sidelined cash pile isn't growing to meet this.

Sentiment sits at 71, Greed, near the top of its own 30-day range of 25 to 72. That the gauge is pinned near its high while RSI readings are pinned near overbought and whale wallets are sending coins to exchanges is not a contradiction to explain away, it's the read: the crowd feels good, momentum is stretched, and the on-chain flow of coins doesn't agree with the ETF tape. What to watch from here: whether the weekly whale flow prints a third straight onto-exchange week, whether funding on any of these majors flips negative (a real de-risking signal, not just a red daily candle), and whether the ETF five-session net breaks its current same-direction streak. Any one of those changing would be worth a second look at this setup.

Elsewhere in the majors, ADA remains the odd one out below its 200-day and 75.6% off its 12-month high, and Bitcoin dominance at 58.8% shows BTC still commanding the largest share of a total market cap that fell 2.25% over 24 hours to $2.63T. Among the day's movers, TRUMP (+36.5%), STX (+26.0%), and POL (+23.9%) lead gainers while MORPHO (-10.5%), ASTER (-9.0%), and ONDO (-7.0%) lead losers, a reminder that under a broadly green trend structure, individual names are still moving on their own terms.
